# Sandboxes quickstart

A sandbox is a Linux microVM for an agent or for untrusted code. It
starts in well under a second from the pool, runs your commands, holds
files, and serves its ports to you over an authenticated tunnel. The API and SDKs follow
E2B, so most code moves over with a change of import.

Coding agents: run `tritonctl llms.txt` for a guide and an index of every
command, or `tritonctl llms-full.txt` for every flag.

In this guide, `https://api.example.com` is your cloud API endpoint. Your administrator
gives you the real one, your user name and your project.

## Gated features

Some features are off until an administrator turns them on for your tenant.
When a feature is off, the API answers `403 FeatureDisabled` and names
the feature.

| Feature | Default |
|---|---|
| exec, files, stop/start, filesystem snapshot and fork | on |
| port tunnels (`port-forward`) | on |
| preview URLs (with a token) | off until the cloud has a preview domain |
| code interpreter | on |
| templates from an OCI image or a snapshot | on |
| pause/resume, memory snapshot, memory fork | administrator enables |
| desktop, RDP, screenshots and input | administrator enables |
| templates from a Dockerfile | administrator enables |
| egress by domain name (`--allow-out-domain`, `--repo`) | administrator enables |
| public preview URLs (no token) | administrator enables |

`tritonctl sandbox capability` and `Sandbox.capabilities()` show what
your deployment offers.

## 1. Install tritonctl

There is no binary download yet. Build it from source (Rust, Linux; macOS
is not tested yet):

```sh
git clone --branch main https://github.com/TritonDataCenter/mariana-trench.git
cd mariana-trench
git submodule update --init --depth 1 images/triton-platform/manta-storage
cargo install --locked --path cli/tritonctl
```

The repository is private for now. Ask your administrator for read access.

## 2. Log in

```sh
tritonctl configure --endpoint https://api.example.com --project default \
  --username alice --password-stdin
tritonctl whoami
```

If your administrator uses a private CA for the API, set
`TRITON_DC_ANCHORS=ca.pem`. tritonctl and both SDKs read it and add the CA
to the default roots.

## 3. Install an SDK (optional)

Not on PyPI or npm yet.

Python 3.10 or later:

```sh
pip install "git+https://github.com/TritonDataCenter/mariana-trench.git@main#subdirectory=sdks/python"
```

TypeScript (Node 18 or later, or Bun), from the checkout above:

```sh
(cd sdks/typescript && npm ci && npm pack)
cd /path/to/your/project
npm install /path/to/mariana-trench/sdks/typescript/triton-sandbox-0.1.0.tgz
```

The SDKs read the tritonctl session, so after step 2 they need no more
setup. Otherwise set `TRITON_URL` and `TRITON_USERNAME` with
`TRITON_PASSWORD` (or `TRITON_API_KEY`).

## 4. Create a sandbox and run commands

```sh
tritonctl sandbox create --name dev --package sandbox-2g --ttl 1h
tritonctl sandbox exec dev -- uname -a
tritonctl sandbox exec -t -i dev -- bash       # interactive; ~. detaches
tritonctl sandbox list
tritonctl sandbox delete -y dev
```

```python
from triton_sandbox import Sandbox

sbx = Sandbox.create(timeout=3600, package="sandbox-2g")
print(sbx.commands.run("uname -a").stdout)
sbx.kill()
```

A package sets the size. The default set is:

| Package | vCPU | Memory | Disk |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sandbox-2g` | 2 | 2 GiB | 8 GiB |
| `sandbox-4g` | 2 | 4 GiB | 16 GiB |
| `sandbox-8g` | 4 | 8 GiB | 32 GiB |

Without `--package` (`package=` in Python, `package:` in TypeScript and
the MCP `create_sandbox` tool) you get the default package (`sandbox-2g`
unless your administrator set another). Sizes as numbers are refused, and
the error names the packages you can use. To change the size, move the
sandbox to another package: stop it, then `tritonctl sandbox resize dev
--package sandbox-4g` or `sbx.resize("sandbox-4g")` (the disk never
shrinks).
`--on-deadline stop|pause|delete` sets what happens when the TTL runs out;
`tritonctl sandbox keepalive dev --ttl 1h` moves it.

Network egress is denied by default. Open it per sandbox, by address
block or (gated) by domain name:

```sh
tritonctl sandbox create --name web --package sandbox-2g --allow-out <public-cidr>
tritonctl sandbox create --name gh --package sandbox-4g --allow-out-domain github.com --allow-out-domain '*.github.com'
tritonctl sandbox network replace web --allow-out <public-ip>/32    # replaces the whole policy
```

Egress needs a NAT gateway and a default route in your VPC; without one
the policy is refused. Private and internal address ranges are always
refused.

## 5. Files

```sh
tritonctl sandbox fs put dev ./data.csv /work/data.csv
tritonctl sandbox fs ls dev /work          # mode, size, mtime, name; -j for JSON
tritonctl sandbox fs cat dev /work/data.csv
tritonctl sandbox fs get dev /work/out.json ./out.json
tritonctl sandbox fs watch dev /work --recursive
```

SDK: `sbx.files.write/read/list/stat/remove/rename/make_dir/watch`.

## 6. Reach a port

Start a server in the guest (keep that exec running, or use
`commands.run(..., background=True)` in the SDK), then forward its port
to your machine:

```sh
tritonctl sandbox exec dev -- python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1 &
tritonctl sandbox port-forward dev 8000
curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/
```

The tunnel runs over the API with your own credential, so only you
reach the port. It carries any TCP service: a web app, a database, a
debugger. SDK: `sbx.ports.forward(8000)`.

### Preview URLs (coming)

Browser preview URLs (`https://8000-<sandbox-id>.<preview-domain>/`)
are not enabled on this cloud yet. Until they are, `tritonctl sandbox
url`, `sandbox ports open` and the SDK's `get_host`, `get_url` and
`ports.open` stop with "previews are not enabled on this cloud; use
port-forward" (`PreviewsDisabledException` in Python,
`PreviewsDisabledError` in TypeScript). `tritonctl sandbox capability`
lists `preview_urls` as refused.

## 7. Snapshot and fork

```sh
tritonctl sandbox snapshot create dev --name ready
tritonctl sandbox fork dev --count 3 --from-snapshot ready
tritonctl sandbox fork dev --count 3 --kind memory     # gated: running processes too
```

`fork` waits until every child runs and names any child that did not
start; `--no-wait` prints the children at once.

A filesystem fork boots fresh children with the parent's disk. A memory
fork resumes the parent's processes in each child, with its own
hostname, network address and entropy. Secrets already in the parent's
memory are in every child too, so snapshot before you load them.

SDK: `sbx.snapshot(name=)`, `sbx.fork(3, kind="memory")`.

## 8. Stop, pause and resume

```sh
tritonctl sandbox stop dev      # keeps the disk, not the memory
tritonctl sandbox start dev
tritonctl sandbox pause dev     # gated: keeps memory and disk
tritonctl sandbox resume dev
```

SDK: `sbx.stop()`, `sbx.start()`, `sbx.pause()`, `sbx.resume()`.

## 9. Templates

A template is a root filesystem plus defaults (env, start command, ready
check). A template does not set the size: the package does.

```sh
# From an OCI image. ENTRYPOINT/CMD, USER, WORKDIR and ENV are kept.
tritonctl sandbox template build py312 --image docker.io/library/python:3.12-slim --follow

# From a Dockerfile (gated). The context is sent as a tar of at most 1 MiB.
tritonctl sandbox template build api --dockerfile ./Dockerfile --context . \
  --ready-port 8080 --follow

# From a snapshot. No build runs.
tritonctl sandbox template build devbox --from-snapshot dev/ready

tritonctl sandbox create --name t1 --template py312 --package sandbox-4g
tritonctl sandbox template list --builtin
```

A build is queued and the command returns at once. `--wait` prints each
status until the build is ready or failed, and exits non-zero on a failure;
`--follow` also prints the build log.

Private registry: `--registry-user USER --registry-password-stdin`. The
credential is used for that build only. Only amd64 images build.

## 10. Code interpreter

```python
from triton_sandbox import Sandbox

sbx = Sandbox.create(template="code-interpreter")
ex = sbx.run_code("import pandas as pd; pd.DataFrame({'a': [1, 2]}).sum()")
print(ex.text)
ex = sbx.run_code("import matplotlib.pyplot as plt; plt.plot([1, 3, 2]); plt.show()")
png_base64 = ex.results[0].png
```

State lives between calls, as in a notebook. `sbx.create_code_context()`
gives a separate one.

## 11. Desktop and RDP (gated)

```python
sbx = Sandbox.create(template="desktop")
open("screen.png", "wb").write(sbx.desktop.screenshot())
sbx.desktop.left_click(200, 300)
sbx.desktop.type("hello")
sbx.desktop.key("Return")
```

Live view over RDP:

```sh
tritonctl sandbox create --name desk --template desktop
tritonctl sandbox rdp desk --local 13389
```

It prints the user, a one-off password, the certificate fingerprint and an
`xfreerdp` line. Any RDP client works on `localhost:13389`.

## 12. GitHub repo workflow

```sh
tritonctl sandbox create --name app --repo owner/app --branch main
tritonctl sandbox exec app --cwd /work/app -- make test
tritonctl sandbox git app -- switch -c fix
tritonctl sandbox git app -- commit -am "Fix the bug"
tritonctl sandbox pr app --title "Fix the bug" --draft
```

`--repo` needs the egress-domain feature. tritonctl takes the token from
`gh auth token` (or `--github-token-env VAR`) and gives it only to the
git commands that talk to GitHub. It is not stored in the guest. See
[sandbox-github.md](sandbox-github.md) for the details and for
`tritonctl sandbox claude --repo`.

## 13. SSH and VS Code

```sh
tritonctl sandbox ssh-config dev --install
ssh dev.sandbox.triton
scp ./file dev.sandbox.triton:/work/
```

ssh rides the same authenticated tunnel as port-forward, so the guest has
no open port. VS Code Remote-SSH works with the same host name.

## Coming from E2B

The calls map one to one. Change the import and the API key variable.

| E2B (Python) | Triton (Python) |
|---|---|
| `from e2b_code_interpreter import Sandbox` | `from triton_sandbox import Sandbox` |
| `E2B_API_KEY` | `TRITON_URL` + `TRITON_API_KEY`, or the tritonctl session |
| `Sandbox.create(template=, timeout=)` | `Sandbox.create(template=, timeout=)` |
| `Sandbox.connect(id)` | `Sandbox.connect(id)` |
| `Sandbox.list()` | `Sandbox.list(labels=)` |
| `sbx.commands.run(cmd, background=, on_stdout=)` | `sbx.commands.run(cmd, background=, on_stdout=)` |
| `sbx.pty.create(...)` | `sbx.pty.create(...)` |
| `sbx.files.read / write / list / remove` | `sbx.files.read / write / list / remove` |
| `sbx.files.watch_dir(path)` | `sbx.files.watch_dir(path)` (also `watch`) |
| `sbx.get_host(port)` | `sbx.get_host(port)` |
| `sbx.run_code(code)` | `sbx.run_code(code)` |
| `sbx.set_timeout(s)` | `sbx.set_timeout(s)` |
| `sbx.beta_pause()` / `sbx.pause()` | `sbx.pause()` |
| `Sandbox.resume(id)` / `connect` | `Sandbox.connect(id)` (starts or resumes it), `sbx.resume()` |
| `sbx.kill()` | `sbx.kill()` |
| Desktop `screenshot / left_click / write / press` | `desktop.screenshot / left_click / type / key` |
| Desktop `stream` (VNC) | `tritonctl sandbox rdp`, `desktop.rdp_tunnel()` |
| no equivalent | `sbx.snapshot()`, `sbx.fork(n)`, `sbx.stop()`, `sbx.start()` |

Differences that matter:

- Egress is denied unless you allow it (`network=` in the SDK).
- `files.remove()` refuses a non-empty directory unless `recursive=True`.
- Preview URLs are not enabled yet; use `ports.forward` to reach a port.
- A refusal is a typed exception; `NotImplementedException.reason` says
  what the deployment leaves out on purpose.
